content.user_title: Diagnose Bugs With a Reproducible Loop
content.value_statement: Hard bugs waste time when teams guess before reproducing the failure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code from reproduction to regression test.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a deterministic reproduction loop using tests, scripts, browser automation, or trace replay.
Requires confirmation that the loop reproduces the user-visible failure.
Prompts for three to five ranked, falsifiable hypotheses before testing.
Recommends targeted instrumentation with removable debug log tags.
Directs regression testing before the fix when a correct seam exists.
Includes cleanup checks for repros, temporary logs, prototypes, and post-mortem notes.
limitations: It needs project access, fixtures, logs, or captured artifacts to reproduce real failures.
It does not replace domain knowledge from users or maintainers.
The human-in-the-loop script is a template and must be adapted.
Production instrumentation requires explicit permission and careful review.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Application Bugs
use_cases.description: Turn vague bug reports into a deterministic loop, then verify the fix against the original symptom.

use_cases.title: Isolate Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Measure a baseline, rank likely causes, and test one performance hypothesis at a time.

use_cases.title: Structure Debugging Handoffs
use_cases.description: Capture the repro, hypotheses, fix evidence, and prevention notes for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Diagnosis
prompt_templates.scenario: A user reports a clear bug but no investigation has started.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnose skill on this bug. Build a feedback loop first. Reproduce the failure before proposing a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a UI Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: A browser workflow fails and needs a reliable reproduction path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this UI bug. Choose a browser or human-in-the-loop reproduction path. Confirm the visible symptom before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Regression
prompt_templates.scenario: A behavior changed between two versions or commits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnose process for this regression. Build a bisectable signal. Rank hypotheses and test one prediction at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Root Cause Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: A complex bug needs fix evidence and prevention notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this failure end to end. Minimize the repro, test hypotheses, fix it, remove instrumentation, and write prevention notes.

output_examples.input: A test fails only on CI after a dependency update.
output: A local loop that reproduces the CI-like failure.
A ranked hypothesis list tied to dependency behavior.
A regression test plan and cleanup checklist.

output_examples.input: The export button throws an error for some users.
output: A browser or human-in-the-loop reproduction plan.
A request for the exact symptom and affected conditions.
A fix path verified against the original export scenario.

output_examples.input: A page became slower after a recent release.
output: A baseline measurement before any optimization.
Focused probes for likely regression causes.
A final check that performance improved without new failures.

best_practices: Start with the fastest deterministic loop that reproduces the real symptom.
Write falsifiable hypotheses before changing code or adding instrumentation.
Remove temporary logs, prototypes, and debug helpers before declaring the fix complete.
anti_patterns: Changing code before reproducing the original failure.
Logging everything instead of adding probes tied to specific hypotheses.
Adding shallow tests that do not exercise the real bug path.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It gives agents a disciplined process for hard bugs and performance regressions. The process starts with a reliable feedback loop.

faq.question: Does it fix bugs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides investigation, hypothesis testing, implementation, and verification using the project context available to the agent.

faq.question: Can it handle flaky bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on raising the reproduction rate until the failure is frequent enough to debug.

faq.question: Why does it require ranked hypotheses?
faq.answer: Ranked hypotheses reduce guessing. Each hypothesis must predict what evidence would confirm or disprove it.

faq.question: Does it support performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends baseline measurement, targeted profiling, and verification before and after the fix.

faq.question: What access does it need?
faq.answer: It works best with tests, logs, fixtures, traces, or a local environment that reproduces the reported issue.
